persisted_members.where_written: beside the wrapper (/opt/investor-reporting-ycharts/ on the host): last-capture.receipt.json for the newest run, capture-<stamp>-<nn>.receipt.json for the archived runs, each 0600, at most 16384 bytes, ASCII JSON with sorted keys
persisted_members.when_written: by run_capture after the runner's stdout is read, for every run whose receipt carries a login_submission or a probe_pair (failure receipts: record.*; success receipts: record.acquire.*) or a step list; a run that reached neither writes none
probe_pair: with_token_errored (bool, derived from the runner's error message, which is dropped)
without_token_location_present / with_token_location_present (bool, derived: the Location URL is dropped)
without_token_content_type_class / with_token_content_type_class (json|html|other|null, derived: the header value is dropped)

sent_without_token / sent_with_token: cookies_with_values (int), cookie_names (list of names), session_cookie_names_present (list of names), waf_token_cookie_in_jar / waf_token_cookie_sent / waf_header_sent (bool), headers (list of header NAMES), fallback_available (name|null); the user_agent string is dropped
beside_the_two_members: schema, ok, failure_class (closed token), reason (closed token)
steps: list of {step, state, via, probe_reason, probe_via, probe_http_status, probe_state}, at most 16
persisted_members.leaf_rule: a leaf is kept only if it is a bool, an int 0..9999, null, or a string of 1..64 characters from [A-Za-z0-9_.:-] with no 'http' and no run of 16 hex digits or 8 digits; a list keeps at most 16 items; a member not named above is dropped, and so is a named member whose value fails its leaf test

planted_whitelisted_member_with_a_bad_va.username_field: a value with '@' fails the short-name rule
planted_whitelisted_member_with_a_bad_va.login_reply_status: the string '200' is not an integer
planted_whitelisted_member_with_a_bad_va.login_submissions: True is a boolean, not an integer

planted_derived_members.without_token_location: a URL carrying a token query -> without_token_location_present: true
planted_derived_members.with_token_waf_action: a planted password string -> with_token_waf_action_class: other

new_reason_code.name: SIGNED_OUT_APP_CHROME_AFTER_SUBMIT
new_reason_code.fires_when: one sign-in submission was made (filled), the screen is classified CH-AUTHENTICATED by the app-chrome model (via dom or vision, NOT the provisional post-submit reading), and the probe reason is NO_IDENTITY_COOKIE; thrown at the first such probe (step 1 in the replay, MAX_STEPS 8); no second submission, no retry, no added wait. Its record carries login_submission, probe_pair (null here by construction, see the row), the step list, and a screen census with the URL reduced to its path and the page text withheld.

four_postulates.i_mece: Domain: the reasons an AuthError of the capture can carry (9 throw sites after this change, 9 distinct closed reasons, counted by test_every_sign_in_failure_site_carries_its_own_closed_reason). The new code covers the one cell the old pair left open: 'app chrome, probe says no identity cookie' crossed with 'a submission was made' (old SIGNED_OUT_APP_CHROME = not made; new = made); the provisional post-submit screen with no app signal stays with the bounded post-submit probe (ChallengeFailure), and a probe with an identity cookie that still fails stays NO_AUTHENTICATED_PROBE. Subtraction from the 8 pre-existing reasons: none already named 'made + app chrome + no cookie'; none of the 8 overlaps it.
four_postulates.ii_same_grain: Same grain as its sibling SIGNED_OUT_APP_CHROME and the other AuthError reasons: one name per place the sign-in stopped (a screen state plus a probe leg), not a vendor cause and not a remedy; it names an observation the runner made, not an inference about credentials.
four_postulates.iii_one_intent: One axis, one intent: where did the sign-in stop. The code says 'after one submission, the browser holds no identity cookie and the page reads as the app'. It does not say the credentials were rejected (that is SIGNIN_FORM_REPRESENTED, the form came back) and does not say the probe is broken; the persisted login_submission (reply status, field match) is what separates those readings.
four_postulates.iv_state_coherence: The code moves one state: the run ends EXPLICITLY at the first post-submit probe instead of at MAX_STEPS, so it ends the run with one submission spent either way. It does NOT move: the one-refresh-per-job allowance, the 900 s capture cooldown, the lease and fence, the stored session bundle (none is written), and the other reasons' branches. The remedy it points to is a read of the persisted receipt and the account state, never a retry; none of the unchanged branches changes.

token_census.scope: word-boundary token \bSIGNED_OUT_APP_CHROME_AFTER_SUBMIT\b (and the sibling \bSIGNED_OUT_APP_CHROME\b) over the two trees that read reason codes, infra/aws/ec2/investor-reporting-ycharts/ and infra/aws/lambda/investor-reporting/, tracked files at base commit 70412abcd5 (662 tracked files in the two trees) and in the worktree after the change; counts are matching LINES per file; the target is not a substring-safe name (the old name is a prefix of the new one), so the boundary \b after CHROME does not match the new name's underscore

counts.readers_that_enumerate_reasons: host_capture.py validates a reason by pattern (_REASON, [A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{2,63}) and does not list them, so the new name passes through as a closed token with no edit (test_failure_code_names_the_sign_in_step); the only enumerators are test_host_capture.py's throw-site count (8 -> 9 and the distinct-reason count 8 -> 9, on purpose, as its own comment asks) and its parametrised list (the new name added)

stderr_per_run.file_name_rule: newest run: last-capture.stderr (unchanged). On the next run it is renamed to capture-<UTC yyyymmddThhmmssZ of its mtime>-<nn>.stderr, nn two digits rising within one second, so names sort in run order; its receipt takes the same stem with .receipt.json
stderr_per_run.why_16: twice the floor of 8, and more than the 10 sign-in-bearing attempts the 2026-10-11 read counted in 14 days (IB129-1); 16 runs x (64 KiB stderr + 16 KiB receipt) stays under about 1.3 MiB, so the directory is bounded in count (at most 32 files) and in bytes
stderr_per_run.last_capture_name_kept: last-capture.stderr is kept as the newest run's name (STDERR_NAME unchanged; the existing posix test reads it), and last-capture.receipt.json is its sibling; the previous run is archived before the new run opens its file, so a stale receipt never outlives its run
stderr_per_run.unwritable_directory: rotate_runs, stderr_sink, persist_receipt and keep_tail each catch OSError; an unwritable directory sends stderr to DEVNULL and writes no receipt, and the capture still returns or refuses exactly as before (tested)

host_reach: Neither change reaches the host by merging. host_capture.py is a member of the RESIDENT PACKAGE (reports/build_resident_package.py packs ycharts/session/ except tests/ and __pycache__, as ycharts/session/host_capture.py inside the tarball built from a backend pin) and runs only in a resident release under its own never-widen pair, installed as a new /opt/irpt-resident/<pin>-st<N> root. ycharts_session.js and run-ycharts-session.sh are NOT in that tarball: they live in /opt/investor-reporting-ycharts/ on the host (README of that folder; hashed by the wrapper at capture time against the bindings), so ycharts_session.js reaches the host only by a separate install of the file to that directory, and the release's bindings must carry the NEW LIBRARY_SHA256 (a1c2880169c5...) for the pair to agree. Order matters: the new host_capture.py reads a receipt the old library also produces (record.login_submission and record.probe_pair already ride the old NO_AUTHENTICATED_PROBE receipt), so the host_capture.py half is useful alone; the new reason code appears only once the library is installed. run-ycharts-session.sh is unchanged.
